design: MemoryPromotionService implements MemoryPromotionPort (LLD 2.8.1, 2.8.7) for the closed MemoryPromotionRequest of the governed-memory OpenAPI: it validates the binding, the closed request, a trusted-composition registered (proposal_schema_ref, target_aggregate_type) profile that can never be a security or policy type, the GCS digest and the deadline; it reads only the exact committed ACTIVE head through the 0052 eligibility, asks the live promotion policy, re-plans after the policy I/O (stop epoch, source stage digest, deadline) and appends a content-free proposal (source version, item/content digests, evidence and provenance refs, marking, taint, target, GCS digest, stop epoch, deadline) to the protected audit store; it returns exactly the public OperationReceipt (ACCEPTED, audit_ref) and re-validates once more after the audit write.

The memory port has no canonical writer, security writer or mutative memory port; every refusal after the binding is an audited denial and the memory item is never rewritten (ADD v1.3 Part II 2.11: rejected promotion recorded separately).

load(audit_ref) re-reads the recorded proposal, verifies its self-digest and action, and re-runs the full validation under the caller binding with the recorded stop epoch; any change of source, GCS, policy, stop epoch or deadline fails closed with an audited denial.

C6MemoryPromotionConsumer (C6 side of the port) receives only the proposal audit_ref and an authenticated binding. Command, Authority, Decision, approval policy and signatures come exclusively from the separate C6 control authority as one RFC 8785 canonical gate whose signature is verified by an independent verifier (OpenBao transit ed25519 in the qualifying cases).

The gate must bind the exact proposal digest and audit_ref; the command must bind the proposal target, GCS digest, evidence refs and a claim-source binding to the source version, branch main and a gate_package_digest over the whole frozen gate; the Decision must be accepted, live, unrevoked and bound to the command; the Authority is validated with the kernel validate_authority against a delegation verified by C6 delegation admission for this binding (never the Authority's own claim), with Authority and delegation revocation, the composed canonical-commit capability, scope, tenant, domain, compartments, purpose, risk ceiling and bundle; the approvals are validated by the real Human Gate (distinct active humans, roles, separation of duties, TTL, proposer excluded); the live OPA commit decision must permit under the GCS bundle.

Controls are revalidated after the intent audit, after a fresh proposal load and after the last policy I/O (decision window, Authority expiry, Authority/delegation/decision revocation, verified delegation, Human Gate), then C3 is called with the governed command and its receipt is verified against the command; intent and completion are audited.

Before dispatch every refusal is a definite audited denial (commitMemoryPromotion.denied) with a stable detail; after dispatch any error is reported as CONTROL_PLANE_UNAVAILABLE/COMMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and audited as indeterminate, never as success, because the GovernedCommitPort contract does not guarantee that an error means "not committed". A replay of the same gate returns the replayed C3 receipt without a second revision.

Repair cycle 1 audits authentication refusals at the C6 commit entry, with null correlation/GCS until a verified binding exists. Audit unavailability raises AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE. Backend classification is derived from the AST fixture dependency, never from test-name substrings.

Repair cycle 2: authentication denial in propose and load uses only the binding returned by the type-checking authentication boundary, or null until that check succeeds. Invalid objects, mappings and caller-asserted duck bindings never provide correlation/GCS. The real PostgreSQL audit persists each denial; dropping only the per-test audit table proves AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE with no proposal or canonical state success. Authenticated denial preserves verified context.

normative_interpretations: ADD v1.3 Part II 2.11 and LLD 2.8.7 fix the path MemoryItem -> MemoryPromotionProposal -> C6 control/approval/decision -> GovernedCanonicalCommitCommand -> C3. The proposal is recorded in the protected audit store and is never an Approval, Decision, Authority, CapabilityLease or ActionCommand; the C6 consumer is a separate composition with its own control authority, so a request member can never carry a control.

Targets are restricted to explicitly registered profiles; Authority, Delegation, Approval, Decision, CapabilityLease, ActionCommand, Policy, PolicyBundle, Capability and Identity can never be registered (no capability grant or policy mutation through memory). This is the most restrictive reading of "Memory non concede Authority, Approval, Decision, CapabilityLease o ActionCommand".

A C3 error after dispatch is classified indeterminate (reconciliation by reading C3), the fail-closed reading of a port contract that does not distinguish a refused transaction from an unknown outcome.
The OperationReceipt returned by proposeMemoryPromotion carries status ACCEPTED: acceptance of a proposal record, not of canonical state; canonical state exists only with a verified C3 CommitReceipt.

Backlog requirement BR-003 is the generic task requirement; following the sealed G5 practice the cases are also bound to FR-053 (governed admission of canonical state), FR-118 (promotion tests of ADD v1.3 Part II section 3) and FR-119 (revocation and kill-switch races) as component-level evidence only; G6 binding of FR-053 remains with OCOR-DEV-0061.

requirement_results.command: proposeMemoryPromotion records a content-free MemoryPromotionProposal bound to the exact committed source version, GCS, registered target profile, evidence and provenance in the protected audit store and returns only the public OperationReceipt; no ledger, canonical or security write; requests smuggling authority, approval, decision, capability, policy, content or effect members, unregistered or security/policy targets, malformed envelopes, a missing binding or a foreign GCS are refused with an audited denial; on PostgreSQL 16, Qdrant and OpenBao the proposal is durable and revalidated by fresh adapters

The proposal policy (unit fixture faults labelled as such; separate live cases query pinned OPA with allow/deny, a real refused TCP connection, an installed new bundle revision and an installed non-boolean result), deadline, audit availability, proposal integrity and the source eligibility are checked at proposal and again at consumption: revocation, correction, expiry, stop-epoch change (also during policy I/O), policy change, deadline, unrecorded, tampered or foreign proposals fail closed with an audited denial and no proposal; on the real backends revocation, supersession, foreign compartment, stop and policy denial leave only the denial and an unchanged ledger

On PostgreSQL, Qdrant, OpenBao transit (ed25519 gate signature), the real Human Gate and live OPA, a recorded proposal reaches canonical state only through the signed C6 gate (command, Authority, Decision, approvals) and a governed C3 commit whose receipt is verified against the command; the ledger is unchanged, intent and completion are audited, the replay returns the same C3 receipt without a second revision; a C3 refusal or a receipt not bound to the command after dispatch is an audited indeterminate outcome, never success

Missing/unverified bindings produce a durable denial with no C3 revision or outbox row; audit failure fails closed (local failure handling). Each live fault mutates exactly one control of the otherwise accepted gate and is refused before C3 with its own stable detail, leaving canonical state absent, the memory ledger unchanged and an audited denial: missing, unsigned or digest-forged gate; proposal, target, GCS, evidence or claim binding; Authority ref, expiry, not-yet-valid, revocation, purpose, tenant, capability, scope, domain, compartments, risk, self-vouched or unverified or revoked delegation, capability not composed for C3; Decision rejected, expired, revoked, other action or ref; approvals absent, below quorum, self-approved, wrong role, expired, missing required role, expiring during the last policy I/O; OPA deny, outage, stale bundle; stop, source revocation or Decision revocation during policy evaluation

End-to-end component path MemoryItem -> MemoryPromotionProposal -> C6 Policy/Authority/Approval/Decision -> GovernedCanonicalCommitCommand -> C3 on the real backends, with no direct memory write, capability grant or policy mutation at the port or integration level

residual_risks: The C6 control authority, its signer and the proposal audit store of the qualifying cases are test adapters on the real PostgreSQL and OpenBao; no production C6 authority service exists yet, so gate authenticity rests on the independent signature verification plus the store boundary (open, unassigned).

The last control revalidation and the C3 commit are not atomic with respect to a concurrent stop, revocation or approval withdrawal: the current GovernedCommitPort has no stop/epoch fence (open, tracked toward FGM-17; not claimed closed).

canonical_delta is decided and signed by C6 reviewers; this task binds it to the proposal by source version, evidence and claim-source binding, not by semantic equivalence with the memory content (content is never copied into the proposal).

The Authority signature is attested by the signed gate (signature_verified=True after the gate verification) rather than by a separate Authority signature check; acceptable only while the C6 signer is the single trusted authority (open, unassigned).
Proposal and gate digests in audit are non-content references that may be correlatable; the membership-inference risk declared in 0055 remains open and unassigned.
